# Chapter Two: Orah

> *"One knows he has found love when sleep escapes him because reality has finally become better than your dreams."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

Marcus slowly awoke, the smell of spices and cooking meat permeating the simple rustic room, the scent causing his stomach to hitch with excitement at the prospect of eating again.

Slowly sitting up, he breathed in the delicious aroma as his eyes studied the small room he now found himself in, throughout the space was a collection of simple handmade furniture covered lovingly with animal skin and leather wrap, next to the bed he found himself in was a tree stump for an end table, across the top of the polished wood surface was a pitcher of water and a stack of old bandages, noticing the old stained bloody rags and the number of cups sitting out, his face creased into a frown, how long have I been here he wondered.

Returning his attention to the large room he noticed the strange looking oil lamps lining the walls, their low light barely keeping the darkness at bay, giving the room a rustic and earthy feel, as he continued to survey the space, his eyes came upon the centerpiece of the old cabin, along the far wall stood a large stone hearth its rocky rounded structure climbing the entire wall and through the old open A-frame roof.

The small house had a simple warmth about it he thought smiling as he breathed in the homey feel of the home, he felt safe for the first time in a long time he reflected.

His smile quickly fading as he recalled the porch.

How did I get in here, how long ago was that? he wondered, his eyes now ignoring the house and instead looking for its owner

A creaking from above caught his attention, looking up he watched as a pair of small handmade shoes stepped onto what Marcus first thought were tree branches, after a moment he noticed the ties and crossbars making the structure of a ladder, just one made of tree branches he realized as he followed the descending individual.

A young woman, her raven hair was pulled back revealing the soft alabaster skin of her neck and a delicate jawline came into view, upon seeing him sitting up she nearly lost her balance as she gasped in shock, after a moment she regained her composure and with eyes locked on his the maiden finished descending the ladder, Marcus dared not say a word for fear of startling the young woman again and sending her sprawling onto the floor.

She was beautiful, garbed in a simple home-made dress that looked a size too big for her frame, standing at the bottom of the ladder she studied Marcus with a mixture of interest and fear, neither spoke for a moment as they regarded each other, finally Marcus broke the silence “Thank you, for helping me” he said, his words almost too loud in the small quiet home. For a time, the young woman just stood there, cocking her head and studying Marcus “tooric com burish?” she said, the words seemed a question as she paused for an answer.

The language was not familiar to him and with a breath of frustration, Marcus shook his head “I don’t know what you’re saying” he pleaded shrugging to add emphasis to the words, the woman paused, thinking for a moment and then with her hands she made a gesture, one hand forming a bowl and the mock holding a utensil and as she motioned an eating gesture, Marcus understood and nodded “Yes, I am hungry” he finished and the young woman smiled seeming to understand the intent of his answer, turning she walked towards the large hearth.

As she made her way to the fire Marcus looked to the walls watching as the light of the fire danced over the stone, shadows jumping and bobbing as if locked in a vibrant dance across the dark wooden walls.

He rose from the bed and as the sheet fell, he quickly realized he was completely naked under the blanket the heat rose in his face and quickly glanced to ensure he had not been noticed.

Marcus continued to survey the simple surroundings looking frantically for his clothes, she must have dragged him in, undressed him and cleaned his wounds he thought noticing no sign of another person.

“Hello?” He called, the woman turning and nodding at him. “Olaum tripa biuyo” she said cocking her head in confusion when she saw him half out of bed.

“I need clothes” before stopping himself, she doesn’t speak English idiot he chided himself and tried to come up with a way to mime clothes, he failed and simply looked under the blanket and then back at her with a helpless expression she stood there for a moment and then he face brightened with recognition, lightly slapped her forehead she grabbed a grey set of clothes off of a chair, bringing them over and handing them to Marcus.

He couldn’t help but notice that she stayed out of his reach as if she were afraid, he would snap her up. I will have to keep that in mind, he thought as he moved slowly and deliberately trying his best not to seem hostile or scare her.

Marcus studied the simple pants and shirt, they were simple clothes, the seams hand sewn but sturdy, looking up he nodded and smiled at the young woman “Thank you” he said, she smiled at him as if understanding the gesture and returned to the hearth, allowing Marcus to dress in peace.

The clothes were comfortable if a little big, moving his arms he tested the movement and nodded with approval.

Once dressed he stripped the bed and gently folded the linen, laying it on the end of the bed, he would have to figure out how to ask her where she washes clothes at, he thought turning to find her looking at him.

She gave him an appreciative nod before returning to the hearth and the black cast iron pot beginning to boil. Slowly stirring the source of the delicious aroma, she busied herself cooking as Marcus stood there feeling like a third wheel, watching the woman go through the simple domestic steps.

Once she was done, the young woman motioned Marcus to the table where he found a seat and waited patiently as she carried food over and laid out the meal, sitting, the woman chose a seat directly opposite Marcus and it did not go unnoticed, again he got the feeling she was apprehensive about having a man in her home.

Leaning forward to get her attention Marcus placed his hand on his chest, patting it “I am Marcus” he said, as she sat there regarding him with curious eyes looking from him to his hand.

Pausing Marcus repeated the motion and the words. After a moment, a spark of recognition shown in her eyes and she placed a hand on her chest. “Orah,” she answered.

“Your name is Orah?” He asked excitedly as she nodded in response.

Pointing at him she formed the words with difficulty finally saying, “Um du Mahcoos”.

“Close enough” he laughed smiling at the young woman. Orah turned and pointed at the pot “unry?” she asked casting a glance back at him. “Hungry” he said and nodded his head rubbing his stomach and repeating his word “Hungry”.

She understood that gesture and getting up she quickly produced a wooden bowl, filling from the pot then tentatively took a few paces towards him, again staying out of his reach extending the bowl to him, as if he would snap a handout and grab her.

Marcus kept his movements slow and deliberate, taking the bowl and making eye contact “Thank you” he said. The young lady’s face lit up and his breath caught in his chest, she was beautiful he thought as she nodded furiously /

They completed the meal in a companionable silence, afterwards Orah laid out new bedding, putting her hands on the pile, she pointed at him tapping it as she then placed her hands next to her head.

“Guess I have been invited to stay” he said in a low tone. laying a hand on his chest, Marcus lowered his head with a solemn expression, giving her as heartfelt a thank you as he could muster the gesture seeming to transcend the language barrier as her face brightened. As he began to make the bed, he heard her cross the room, followed by the protests of the wooden ladder as Orah made her way to the bedroom.

Lying in bed that night Marcus thought of the simple existence this woman lived in, he had not expected this, nor could he have anticipated it, gone where the marvels of technology he had been familiar with, what happened to his world he wondered, eventually his eyes grew heavy and sleep took him as his body relaxed in the warm shelter of this woman’s home.

He knew where he was even before his eyes opened as the familiar sound of the waves came to him and he tensed with anticipation, opening his eyes the same cliff filled his vision as once again he looked out among the dark torrential waves of the ocean.

This is getting old he thought turning, knowing she would be there as he laid eyes on the woman, standing tall and regal in the red dress as those ice blue eyes regarded him evenly. He watched as those cold eyes narrowed stepping forward her commanding presence intimidating and her face a mask of stone, giving nothing away as she looked him over once. “You are better, you have found shelter haven’t you” it was more of a statement then a question and Marcus remained stoic, opting to simply eye the woman then give anything away.

Something about this method of communication allowed her to divine a lot more than he could, was it simply knowledge he wondered, was there an ability for him to do the same, if so how his mind continued as they both stood there silently neither wanting to be the first to flinch.

Clearing his mind Marcus reached out, like he had with the crystals, trying to divine something from the woman, at the corners of his mind he felt anger and impatience, the woman’s eyes went a little wider for a moment and then suddenly the feelings were gone, as if they had never been there.

She is able to shield herself, then I should be able to he thought, but how his mind raced but came up with nothing, before he could dive into this problem, the woman spoke

“You are not safe fallen one, anyone who shelters you is in danger, many will search for you, they will not care who they hurt, or who they have to kill to find you, and find you they will, tell me where you are, let me help you” she pleaded but he could still hear that edge of impatience and annoyance he had felt, this is not a person who is used to asking for anything he mused still remaining silent, simply watching her as she continued.

“Tell me where you are, I will ensure those with you are not harmed, before it’s too late” the last part of the sentence sounding like a threat and looking into her eyes, he could see it was meant as such. Marcus focused on the area, trying to figure out where they were, was it a real place he wondered looking at the knee-high green grass rolling over small hills for as far as he could see.

Turning he did notice something that he must have missed the last times he had been here, it was small from this distance, probably at least half a mile away he thought as the phallic profile of a lighthouse rose from the cliffs, barely outlined in the waning light of dusk.

“Why must you be so difficult, why cannot you simply tell me where to find you” the woman barked, her patience worn out and Marcus turned back to her, seeing the anger in those icy eyes and smiled despite the look raising his hackles again, this was a woman to fear his instincts told him.

“Because I don’t trust you, I don’t know you and most importantly, you didn’t fucking ask nicely” he said, with the smile never leaving his face, Marcus walked over to the edge of the cliff and simply jumped off, turning as he did and catching the surprised look on the woman’s face before it disappeared, replaced by speeding rock.

Marcus started awake, the room was pitch black, but the fragrance of dinner still hung in the air and he relaxed, trying to calm his hammering heart, there had been a small part of himself despite knowing it was a dream fighting for him to not throw himself off of the cliff, as if doing so would kill him, I am back he thought closing his eyes recalling the latest interaction with the mysterious woman.

She is getting desperate he thought, then he remembered her threat and his eyes opened as he stared to the ceiling, above him Orah slept peacefully, he could hear the steady breathing of the woman as he lay there.

She had taken him in, helped him despite her fear, what right did he have to bring trouble to her door he thought.

Then what would happen if he wasn’t here, what would they do to her to find out where he had gone or any other information, they thought she might have. He shuddered at the thought, this mysterious woman was used to being in charge, she was powerful and if he read her right, someone with the resources to find Orah.

No, he thought, he needed to stay, to protect her, or at the very least let them focus on him and not her should they find him.

What did they want he wondered as Marcus recalled the feeling of abject fear every time, he had encountered her? Whatever it is he thought, I want no part of it and with that thought he settled in and allowed sleep to take him once again.

The next morning, he awoke to the sound of pots and pans being put to use as the familiar smell of bacon aroused his senses and brought him back to consciousness. The house in the light of day had a very different feel to it, as the sun filtered in through the thin white curtains, the beams of light showcased a colorful and vibrant living space, fresh violets sat in simple wooden vases throughout the house, there placement complimenting the various paintings of fields and horses hung along the rustic wooden walls.

Someone was a painter he thought swinging his legs over and onto the cold planked floors.

The stiffness in his joints forced him to pause before removing himself fully from the bed, when he did finally get up, Marcus made the bed and dressed in the clothes from the day before.

Sitting down gently on the edge of the rope bed, his mind now quiet, once again he felt that strange vibration, the one that had been his constant companion during the latter part of his journey through the wilderness, it still called to him, beckoning and inviting, cocking his head he closed his eyes, he would find out what that was, but not right now he thought thinking of the woman.

Marcus had indeed returned to earth, going over the contents of the small cabin and the clothing and equipment he could recall from the riders, this earth was far different than the one he had left, it had reverted to a more primal existence he thought or simply had he landed in some backwater country and any moment helicopters and soldiers would come to retrieve him.

He didn’t not know, the language barrier currently prevented him from finding out those answers; the pod was supposed to bring him down in the western part of North America along with about Twenty thousand other people, but I was late to the party he thought with a bitter smile, if Sentinel was to be believed then based on the timeline, the world was now filled with the descendants of his fellow volunteers, Marcus felt like a man out of time.

Why had he landed late, Sentinel had talked about a malfunction, some reason his pod and a few others were launched late, well centuries late he reflected, did that mean there were others here like him he wondered.

His thoughts turned inevitably to the beautiful young woman who had become his savior don’t get attached Marcus, you don’t know where you are or where this is, you will only strive to either hurt her, or hurt both of you he thought, but it was hard not to think about her, something about the woman had entranced him and it was not easily shaken off.

He needed to break the communication gap with this woman, he had to find out when and where he was, he needed to understand the history he had missed during his sleep.

He needed facts not suspicions, this fear would do nothing to help his situation he reflected. He had so many questions that needed answers, Where did he fit into this world? what kind of world was this? When was this?, what had happened to his world? The questions kept coming, his mind trying to keep up as he mentally listed them. Putting the thoughts away Marcus went to the main room of the house, as soon as he entered, Orah entered from her bedroom, in her arms she carried an assortment of items, he watched curiously as she carefully went about lining up the items on the dining table.

What the hell is she up to he wondered, turning she jerked with a start, realizing that Marcus was indeed awake, with a sigh of relief her face broke into a smile that stopped the young man’s heart.

He made his way over to the hand-carved wooden table, looking curiously at her as Orah straightened a spoon next to a knife, fidgeting for a moment before, with a sigh nodded to him and beckoning him to approach closer.

Picking up the spoon, she showed it to him. “Oon,” she said and then pushed it towards him, he could see the expectant look on her face as she repeated the word. “Oon.”

Marcus cocked his head. “Spoon,” he said.

Orah shot him a frustrated look taking the spoon and holding it out again. “Oon,” she repeated. Marcus formed the unfamiliar word. “Oon,” he said.

Her brilliant smile brightened the room, and he couldn’t help but return it, now understanding what she was up to. Picking up the knife, she said, “Fey,” then shook the knife at him.

He said the word, and Orah put it down, nodding in approval. They continued this throughout the day, her finding an item, saying a word and him repeating it.

Then she would go back to an earlier item and try to get him to remember the word.

He was really bad at that and it took four times through the items before he started to get the names. It was odd he thought they were close to the names he knew like “spoon” was “oon,” and hungry was “ungry”, a linguist would have a field day working out the roots of the language and mapping the words to the original source languages from old earth he reflected with a smile as they continued the exercise.

The language was close to English, with some Spanish and German thrown in he thought, there were a few words he didn’t even come close to recognizing, but if the Sentinel was correct then it was very possible that at one time this new language had started out from an amalgamation of the languages of Old Earth as he now thought of it.

He squashed his errant thoughts, focusing on the lessons, he had to learn to speak to Orah he needed to able to ask simple questions he thought, Orah continued to scour the small house finding items and brandishing them, once he had said the word, she would place the item on the table to come back to later.

He managed to remember chair as she pointed one out and she shot him another approving smile. He had started to notice that when she did that, his stomach would flutter.

Stop that, he thought, chiding himself, trying unsuccessfully to only concentrate on her teaching. It’s not helpful dammit. You’re like a teenager, Grow the fuck up.

By the time night began to descend over the small farm they were both exhausted, but the sense of accomplishment caused both to smile, he could successfully identify about a quarter of the items in the cabin without a hint from Orah.

Marcus felt like the dumb kid in class despite the progress made, if he wished to actually have a conversation with her, then he would have to do much better he admonished himself.

Watching as Orah began to walk around the room turning on the lanterns.

He stopped and did a double-take, she hadn’t used anything to light them he thought, simply turning a knob on the side, did they use batteries he wondered hope he had been wrong about the technology sprung into his mind, wandering over to one of the small lanterns hanging on a wooden hook near the wall he looked it over.

Studying the simple tin housing and hand-blown glass, it looked like a typical kerosene lantern until he opened the small access door, staring dumbfounded he tried to make sense of the simple mechanism.

Sitting within the light chamber were two crystals, suspended on wires with a metal screw, Marcus turned the knob and watched as one of the crystals drew nearer to another and as it did, they both began to glow.

The closer he pushed them by turning the nob, the higher they glowed. “What the hell” he whispered turning the knob the other way, the screw separating the glowing rocks, the further they moved the more the glow diminished returning them to a dark purple and dark blue rock.

There were no wires nothing that plugged into the wall causing this phenomenon, it was just two crystals he realized taking the lantern down and staring at it in wonder.

He gawked at the simple mechanism for a long time, trying to understand the science behind the basic creation, so many things had changed he reflected, the feeling of being lost returning since he had come into this woman’s home, he turned the simple key and then turned it back, watching the crystals glow and then fall dark as he did.

Marcus let Orah know he was going to retire using as much pantomiming as he could, looking at her he had no idea if she understood, but he was sure once he went over and laid on the bed, she would get it.

Orah smiled at him, moving around the room and dimming some of the lanterns, once done, she retired to her room, closing the door, leaving Marcus to the darkness and ultimately to his thoughts.

Sitting there in the low light He felt utterly alone in this new world he now found himself, this world of crystals that glowed and snakes that flew. What else had changed he wondered looking over to the strange lantern again.

The dream did not return that night allowing him a peaceful night of sleep.

He was stared awake by a clattering of pans and the most beautiful voice he had ever heard as an ethereal song floated through the cabin.

He lay there for a while listening to Orah sing and appreciating the voice allowing it to take his mind away from his thoughts from the night before. Rising from bed he walked over towards the hearth, appreciating the growing warmth as he moved closer.

As he approached, she turned with a start Marcus smiled, putting up his hands in a surrender gesture “I didn’t mean to scare you” he said gently and she matched his smile, again his stomach fluttered, and he silently admonished himself for his reaction.

“Uj sian momoa” she said, motioning him over to the table as she began laying out a breakfast of what looked like eggs and potatoes in a bowl, sitting he allowed her to serve him, soon they were eating in companionable silence, Marcus feeling truly at peace for the first time since he could remember, the simple act of eating with another person calming his mind and easing the chaos that plagued him.

Tasting the yellow substance, he thought it might be eggs, but the flavor was a little odd, not bad, just not what he was used to. But he scarfed it down and quickly got up to get more but Orah beat him to it, grabbing his bowl and filling it again, when she placed it in front of him their hands touched for a moment and he felt electricity pass between them, by the way Orah jumped she had too. “Thank you” he said shyly, not meeting her eyes, the young woman blushed and nodded.

“We are going to need to find a way to communicate” he sighed, wishing they had a copy of Rosetta Stone for whatever the hell language she was speaking.

Marcus and Orah spent the time after breakfast once again going over the items as he slowly progressed in learning the words, building off of the previous days lesson he was getting better at remembering items, now they practiced on putting words together, not quite sentences, but enough so that he could verbalize basic concepts.

The similarity to English helping slightly he mused. Before noon Orah emerged after dressing, freshly bathed from the morning chores and lessons she came to sit at the table, where Marcus toiled fixing a broken butter churner at her request.

He understood the concept, but had never seen one, after twenty minutes of trial and error he was able to repair the handle getting it reseated to the plunger giving it a few test pulls he proudly declared it fixed which elicited a giggle from the young woman.

With a triumphant smile he continued to push and pull listening as the plunger moved smoothly in the wooden chamber, making sure the handle did not separate.

Orah sat there, her large blue eyes regarding him with a gentle smile. She got his attention as he put the churn down, turning to focus on her she began motioning to him, gesturing with her hands as she tried to convey something.

It took Marcus almost thirty minutes to get the full concept of what she was asking, He forced down the excitement as he put mental words to her motions, she wants me to stay he thought.

It took another few hours for him to understand the conditions, he would work and sleep in the barn, but she would feed him.

He accepted almost immediately, excited about the prospect, the two spent the day working through the specifics, which was not easy when both didn’t speak the same language, but they muddled through.

Night finally settled over the land as he sat on the top step of the porch, a simple cotton shirt pulled tight over his body, not offering much protection from the cold wind that blew from the east as he surveyed the woods on the edge of the little farm.

He sat there happy but conflicted, part of him wanting to stay, needing to if he was honest with his feelings about the young woman, he also wanted the regularity of routine, the comfort of a warm hearth, someplace safe to lay his head his mind continued, looking towards the woods he closed his eyes, the thrumming that had been his constant companion still emanated from the west, beckoning to him, pulling him towards the sirens call, there was a part that desperately wanted to know what that was and why it called to him he admitted.

He had convinced himself he was helping her, but he knew, the real reason he wished to stay was simple, he was falling in love with the girl that had become his savoir and his friend.

The rest of the afternoon Orah took him around the farm enthusiastically showing him the animals and chores that he would perform. Even with minimal words and frequent hand gestures, he grasped the basics. She took him to the barn, showing him the ladder to the loft and leaving him to explore his new room as she left to prepare for dinner.

The sun was still high in the sky but would be settling behind the horizon in the next few hours he thought realizing the day had gotten away from them. Climbing the simple ladder, taking cautious steps as the old wood creaked under his weight, he crested the old loft and found a dusty alcove, filled with old farm equipment and broken furniture, it would take work but he could turn this into a home, a place to lay his head, it was safe and it was shelter and right now that was more than he could hope for.

The next few hours filled his time with sweeping out the loft and using some twine he had found making a bed out of hay, the messy heap ugly, but comfortable he thought staring at the mass of hay laying on the loft floor.

Something stirred in the corner of the old barn, crossing the floor as he tried to stare into the growing shadows, something burst from behind a box, Marcus’s heart stopped as he raised his hand towards the thing to defend himself and as if the mass of fur had hit a wall it stopped in midair, then hurdled to the left landing near the far wall. Marcus stared unbelieving from his hands to the barn cat that now stood regarding him coolly.

He had felt the pressure of the creature pushing against his palms before pushing back with his mind, then, instantly the pressure had released as the cat had been thrown across the room, he had wished it, thought it and it had happened.

“What the fuck” he whispered looking at his hand and then to the cat, which proceeded to groom itself with complete disinterest. He sat heavily on the edge of the makeshift hay mattress the heady smell of alfalfa and horse permeating the room, he tried to make sense of what had happened, shakily he extended his hand towards a shelf, where a small line of rocks had been placed and reaching out with his mind he could feel the resistance of each item, feel the contour of it from across the room as if he were putting his fingers directly against them.

It was almost surreal he mused pushing lightly against the rock with his mind, his fingers flexing unconsciously as he did, the rough contours of the surface registering against the tips of his fingers.

The resistance of the object a physical feeling despite the distance, increasing his concentration and directing his will Marcus watched as the softball-size piece of quartz slid across the floor the glass-like particles on its surface glinting against the light of the small lantern, the scraping of the rock loud in the silent room.

What is wrong with me? he wondered, frightened as he extended his hand once again, the tremor of fear evident along its surface as another rock slid, coming to rest next to the first

First the thrumming, he thought still hearing the sound as it echoed from the west, then the dream and now this. Something is wrong with me, what did they really do to me at ARC his mind continued.

Another item scraped along the floor as he extended his hand absently. What am I? Am I even still human? he wondered. Another rock sliding across the floor to join the others, I need to find out what happened to me he finished.

Marcus stood up from the floor, dusting off the cotton pants and collecting the items. The short journey from his position to the objects settled the question in his mind, he could not tell Orah or anyone until he found out more, he could not bear the look on her face. Would she think me a monster? he wondered.

Marcus crawled into bed, pulling himself into a fetal position, the cold night biting into his body as he pulled an old horse blanket over himself, tolerating the itch of the thick wool as it began to warm his body, protecting him from the cold.

The following weeks went by fast as Marcus focused on the chores, his proficiency at feeding and caring for the animals growing daily, giving him a feeling of accomplishment and purpose.

In the evenings Orah would teach him the language, Marcus learning small phrases at first and then his dialog continuing to grow, in fact he was surprised at his ability to pick up the language and after a month and a half he could hold a basic conversation with his hostess.

It was during these little sessions that Marcus had learned that Orah was indeed alone, her parents having died of fever two years before. He had decided to go with a general story telling her he was a traveler from far away who had gotten lost.

Once in a while Orah would catch him sitting on the fence near the barn staring at the sky or looking to the west, a look of longing or concern on his face.

Marcus did his best to hide the sadness and fear at the discovery of his abilities, when he thought about all he had lost and what he could now lose should his ability come to light he cringed with fear, since landing, since his journey he had no greater fear then that of being alone, it shaped his entire being.

Orah could see the worry and fear etched on his face and though she gently pressed he would not talk about it the topic becoming almost taboo between them. Once she asked about it, about his past and he quickly changed the subject, she had allowed it, but he could see Orah was curious.

As the days grew shorter, the weather grew colder, allowing them to spend more time together, Marcus getting better by the day learning the language.

At night he would close himself in the barn before sleep and practice with his new abilities, pushing bigger and bigger objects, never telling Orah about his growing ability or the thrumming, or even the dreams that still plagued him every so often.

One night he finally decided he had enough grasp of the language to ask the questions which had burned in his mind for almost four months. He had thought over the best way to find out what had happened and finally had settled on a very general approach. Orah sat in her chair, the firelight dancing over her face as she concentrated on a shirt she was repairing.

Approaching, he stopped a moment and appreciated the way the light played over her features. She is breathtaking, he thought again for the thousandth time and then dismissed it.

He refused to make her feel uncomfortable, she was a woman alone and quite probably did not need him complicating their situation he once again chided himself.

Taking a seat across from her, he waited as she continued to stitch a line along the seam.

Finally, Orah looked up, her deep blue eyes regarding him with curiosity “What is it? “she asked in her native tongue. “I want you to tell me your history” he responded in the same tongue his mastery of the language was basic and broken, but acceptable and she smiled with pride at his use of it.

“You’re getting better Marcoos, you speak less like a toddler each day” she said teasingly, and he rolled his eyes not bothering to correct her on her pronunciation of his name.

“Why would you like to know history? surely there are more useful things to know” she asked arching an eyebrow at him teasingly. Marcus did his best to ignore how incredible sexy it made her look when she did that.

“I am interested in it, and I would know where your people came from” he finally said, using the term your people in keeping with his traveler story. She sat back, collecting her thoughts.

“Our history comes from the church, more stories than history, but I will tell you what I know, we live in the second age of humanity” she began, and Marcus leaned forward listening with rapt attention as she continued.

“Long ago the earth was inhabited by the ancients, humans who were more like gods then men, they built great machines to do their bidding, finding no need to perform menial tasks they set their inventions to work and instead they would focus on loftier, more intellectual pursuits” she continued, stopping to look over and see if Marcus was still listening, he had allowed his mind to drift a little, thinking of Sentinel and the AI still in orbit, it dawned on him she wasn’t talking and he looked over to see a worried look on her face shit he thought not wanting to share his thoughts, smiling he nodding at her to continue, the worried look lingered for a moment and he again, motioned for her to continue.

“The four gods of the world got angry at the hubris of man as they tore into the world with abandon, gathering more and more of the worlds resources, destroying the paradise the gods had built for their own greedy pursuits, these ancients no longer believed in the gods, they worshipped the machine and gold, amassing great fortunes at the expense of the planet, in fact they believed themselves to be the masters of the earth and this angered the gods.

Man had scarred the planet for generations, killing plants and animals for profit and sport, spurning the creations of the gods abusing the precious resources,the gifts of the earth, with no concern of the damage they did, the four gods came to a decision, that man had become a hazard and needed to be removed, turning to juo, god of thunder and the greatest weaponsmith in the heavens, they commissioned a machine, a death machine, unleashing it on the world, the gods, removed man destroying any trace of them and their creations, erasing any trace of these would be gods, leaving no trace of the ancients or the monuments to their vast empire.

The earth was purged, returned once again to the animals, the planet eventually healed and it was once again peaceful and lush, but the gods quickly became bored, lonely, missing the worship of man, time softening the crimes of humanity, the four gods once again met, deciding to bring back man, but to never again suffer the technology that had replaced them, they would bring man to the earth once again, more importantly they would once again worship the gods, but they would not allow them to create there great machines, should they do that, the machine would once again return to remove man, they sent forth man in tears of metal to repopulate the planet, as punishment they gave them the knowledge of the technology but not the ability to create it, man had once again returned to the earth but without the basic knowledge of how to survive, it was an age of darkness an death, it took many generations for man to begin to live as one with the earth again, to learn once again how to survive, they were like children without the knowledge to survive.

One of the four gods Gorlin, felt guilty at the annihilation of Mankind and the punishment the gods had bestowed on them, stripping them of the knowledge of survival, forcing them to relearn it like babes in the woods and had set about to give mankind a gift, soon they discovered the god Gorlin had bestowed his powers upon them, the ability to bend the world to their will with thought.

These humans wandered the world for ages, banding into small tribes fighting for land, resources or simply honor, the wisest were killed first to prevent other tribes from gaining an advantage, once again, humanity was at the brink of extinction until finally a great ruler emerged from the masses, his name was Aurtus, he fought for many years to bring the tribes of man together, as one people and eventually succeeded, his legacy became one of peace and prosperity as he became our first Emperor.

The gods were so impressed that upon his death, rose Aurtus up to the heavens making him our emissary, his job is to ensure that we never forgot the lesson of the ancients and that we did not repeat their mistakes” she finished.

Marcus sat there stunned it sounded as if she had read that somewhere “Is that a passage or a parable?” he asked the tempo with which she spoke was as if she were repeating the story of Noah from the Old Testament.

Orah smiled “The messenger speaks of it on Son when my parents used to take me to assembly, it’s kind of a summation of what they say, you should talk to the messenger, they tell it better, I glossed over much of the story” she said with a sheepish grin.

Son, he translated in his head. Sunday. The rest day, he thought and nodded.

“Who is the messenger and what is assembly?” he asked hope creeping into his voice. She had stated enough truth in the story that there might be someone who knew the whole story he thought, this messenger perhaps, well minus the god’s stuff.

She cocked her head and looked at him with an odd expression as if he had asked what the sky was.

Marcus quietly contemplated the story, he knew the plan that had been laid out for ARC, there were hints within her story of the landing of his compatriots, could it be possible that buried in the religious rhetoric was the truth of what happened to earth and the chronicles of the landing, he thought about it, yes he was sure of it, if he could remove the god stuff he might be able to get an accurate idea of what happened.

It wasn’t lost on him the story included powers and abilities, he thought about his own discovery, was it possible that those that returned, those like him had also been changed.

He needed to find out more he reflected keeping these thoughts to himself as he regarded the beautiful creature across from him, imagining the look of horror on her face once he revealed his ability to move items without touching them he had wanted to tell her, share with her the change, he wanted to have someone to talk to about it, but instead he continued to keep that to himself, the fear of judgement greater then the need to share.

“The Messenger of Aurtus, the one who speaks his words, assembly is when the sun is at its highest, we gather at the keep hearing him speak the truths” she said breaking into his thoughts.

“Tell me more about this religion,” he asked. Continuing to listen attentively as she explained, by the end of the conversation he had the basics, there were four gods, one for each season and Aurtus, first Emperor and now the emissary to the gods, ensuring that the mistakes of the ancients were not repeated. There was more but most of it was about the ceremonies and incantations the messenger used during the mass or assembly. Marcus thought back over the story, there was a history buried in there, one he recognized, he needed to pursue this, try to reconstruct fact from fiction.

“Can we attend assembly?” he asked surprising himself almost as much as he did Orah with the question, she took a moment thinking on it before finally nodding.

They didn’t speak about it anymore that night, instead discussing the farm and chores and what still had to be done before the first snowfall.

They continued to grow closer and more comfortable with each passing day, four days before they were set to attend assembly Marcus began to suspect Orah might share his feelings for her, but he didn’t dare ask, what if he was wrong he thought, he could easily destroy the incredible friendship that had been built between the two of them, every morning he resolved to tell her, to explain how he felt, but by noon he would lose his nerve, the value of the friendship always outweighing the need to explore a more intimate relationship.

Almost a month had gone by before Orah announced they would be going to Assembly this coming Son, teased by Orah’s words he had waited quietly but impatiently, the announcement causing a minor celebration in his head.

That following Son, when the first rays of sunlight made their way up over the horizon shading the world in a pink glow, the day found Marcus already awake, excited at the prospect of learning more about the history of this world.

He had already been awake for an hour, ensuring the chores were done early, as before they could go anywhere the farm had to be attended to.

Winter was coming and the survival of both of them relied on the harvest in a month, there was meat to smoke and vegetables to can as well as a roof to fix and a few other chores that would determine their ability to survive this coming winter.

By the time Orah appeared out of the little cabin to collect eggs from the henhouse and bacon from the small storehouse, he had already washed and dressed. She smiled at him as he approached the cabin, the same way a mother would a child excited to go to market.

Marcus helped cook and as they ate breakfast, Orah continued to smile at his anticipation for the journey. After the meal was done and the dishes cleaned, Marcus Aided Orah in saddling the two old Mares he had brought in from the field that morning.

He had never even seen a horse saddled and had spent a good twenty minutes chasing the animal around trying to place the leather object on its back as it turned in circles giving him annoyed chuffs.

Orah eventually stopped laughing long enough to help him earning her a mock annoyed look from him.

“You are odd Marcoos, who doesn’t know how to saddle an old Mare” she said shaking her head as they rode out of the farm and heading west.

Ironically enough, towards the thrumming that had been his constant companion since finding himself here, the sound still calling as it grew ever louder the closer, they rode towards town.

He did his best to ignore the sound, pulling the jacket closer to his body as a breeze kicked up the cold morning wind, the days getting colder meant they would have to begin the final harvest soon he thought, allowing the thought to distract him from the constant thrumming.

Had he been there that long, wasn’t it just yesterday that it had felt like early fall when Orah had found him on her doorstep he marveled.

Marcus shook his head at how time passed in the void of the farm, far from the worries except for the crops and the shelter.

His life had narrowed to simple worries and simple pleasures over the past few months and he found it amazing at how easy it was to forget everything beyond the small piece of land.

The countryside lazily passed as the two of them rode in companionable silence Marcus enjoying the skeletal trees, the colorful leaves now covering the ground as the forest braced itself for winter’s first snow.

The air was brisk and smelled of pine and poplar as the two made their way towards the small town.

As they moved closer to town Orah pointed out the local grain mill, where they would bring the harvest before taking it to town and selling it.

She told him the man who owned it had been a friend of her fathers, allowing her to process and crush the wheat and collecting payment once she had sold it.

She spoke of the arguments between the farmers on who would process the wheat first. Those left waiting would inevitably get less for their harvest than those who processed early she explained.

He nodded in appreciation of her knowledge of business, she knew the wheat sold for more once it was processed, allowing her to collect more coin and buy items for the farm.

Helpless she was not he reminded himself, his opinion, like his feelings had grown considerably since that first day seeing the scared young woman, her knowledge, expertise and abilities impressing him almost daily.

As they rode closer to town, the thrumming became harder to ignore, getting louder as the feeling of being called grew steadily by the minute, they were heading right for the source and it was beginning to take all his willpower not to push the horse faster, to reach that sound, to discover its source, He was so distracted by this that it was a good few minutes before Orah pointed out the town as it had come into view and began to grow larger.

Looking up Marcus saw a large circular wooden fence, large trunks of trees had been stood on end and lashed together to create it, the dark brown bark still mostly on the trunks giving the fence an earthy feel. The wall gave the small village the look of a fort instead of a village.

Coming down the hill towards the single entrance, he could see the buildings positioned in a circle all facing inward towards what looked like a worn dirt square with a stone well in the very center, all of the structures save one looked very similar.

All built with that log cabin style, that he was familiar with from movies and TV, that was except the one stone structure which stood out in the small village, this must be the keep he thought to himself. “Why is there a fence?” he asked still studying the structures within.

“Some men don’t live by the tenets of Aurtus” she said simply, an edge in her voice as she spoke, nodding Marcus understood, even in this time there were bandits and thieves, simpler times did not always mean nicer times he reminded himself as they trotted towards the gates of the small village called Tree side.

Coming to the large entrance, Marcus could see the two guards standing sentry. The men were clad in black tunics with what looked like a lioness medallion on them.

Eyeing the dark metal swords and large wooden stocks of the odd-looking rifles that were slung across their backs, he began to get nervous, the feeling illogical, but something about the looming guards bothered him.

The guards looked bored, even their approach had not caused them to alter their relaxed posture in the least, Marcus felt his nervous feeling dissipate at the guard’s lack of reaction to the two of them approaching.

Orah ignored them, instead moving her horse to the right of the entrance where poles had been sunk into the ground. Marcus followed suit as she dismounted her horse expertly and tied it to one of the available posts.

The horse sidling up to the side of the building and began to nibble from a wooden trough.

It took Marcus a few minutes to dismount out of the corner of his eye he could see the guards hiding smirks as he nearly fell on his head trying to get off the old mare.

Orah tried to hide a smile as she came over to hold the horse, allowing him to dismount.

She quickly tied his horse to the same pole, patting it on the side and whispering a few gentle words to the old grey mare.

Marcus still a little embarrassed about his dismount, avoided looking at the guards and instead followed Orah through the gates and into the town, pointedly not listening or reacting to the chuckles from the guards as they passed.

Once inside the wall, he took a moment to eye them out of the corner of his eye watching as the two guards stood whispering and laughing quietly, however Marcus wasn’t interested in there reaction’s anymore.

The rifles had caught his interest, they seemed out of place in an era that looked more medieval than anything else, but he could see the distinct look of early repeating rifles, reminding him of a Henry, the hexagon barrels and ornate lever actions adorned the slung weapons, in a time where I would expect to see bows, instead I find western era firearms, so some expertise existed in certain areas allowing them to progress faster with technology, maybe there was something to the ARC members passing knowledge he thought and then stopped, in a pouch on one of the guards belt he could see a blue glow emanating from the bag.

Turning to Orah he nudged her and nodded his head back towards the guard “What’s in the bag?” he asked, Orah turning and nodding in understanding “The guns ammunition, the crystal resin they used to fire them” she finished. Marcus nodded not knowing what else to say, blue crystal ammunition he thought looking back at the bag, the more things changed he thought, the more they stayed the same.

The guard noticed him eyeing the pouch and turned his body, so it faced away from Marcus.

“Can I help you?” he asked, walking over to bring himself to stand in front of the two, his tone annoyed and Marcus smiled apologetically, slowly he managed to get out the words in the local tongue “I’m sorry, I noticed your rifle and the odd ammunition, I have never seen it’s like, tell me what is it?” He asked and the man cocked his head curiously, Orah began speaking, explaining to the guards that Marcus was a traveler from afar and she repeated his request, his own attempt to broken to be comprehensible he thought.

“Resin rifles, my friend, the crown grows the ammunition from the crystals, a special hybrid formula the weapons master created, they are quite accurate and powerful” he stated proudly, bragging overtly about his weapon.

Marcus nodded and thanked the guard, the man stepping back over to his friend as Marcus followed Orah towards the small-town center.

He noticed the stylized Raven patch over the heart of the tunics while the guard stood before them the lioness over the right breast and the raven over the left, odd he thought thinking they were like unit patches from his time.

“Who are they” he whispered once they were out of earshot of the guards.

Orah shot a disapproving look over her shoulder Marcus catching the flash of anger and the tightening of her mouth as she did “They are the Lord Seer’s guards; they keep the town safe” she whispered but he could hear the undertone of irony in her words, there was a story there he thought, but now was not the time as he stifled his curiosity.

“I get the swords, but the resin rifles were like nothing I have ever seen” he whispered, changing the subject as he leaned in to ensure his voice didn’t carry.

“We use crystals for a lot Marcoos” she said, and Marcus could tell he had reached the limit of her knowledge of it, he would have to ask around if he wanted to know more.

A gun that fired little crystal balls sounded, well cool he thought then he focused on the rest of what she had said.

“Who is the Lord Seer and why don’t you like him?” he asked, and Marcus could tell he hit the nail on the head as she shot him a heated look.

Orah pointed to the hill where the profile of a large stone building stood stalwart as if guarding the town. “Lord Seer Galen Bor is the Reagent of Turen. He runs the province for the Empress, when she married the emperor, she replaced a man who was well respected, Galen is not, he is not a man you want to notice you” she finished and Marcus could tell the subject was closed by the tone of her voice.

He shot the guards one more look as he followed Orah deeper into the town.

As he watched a young boy with tattered clothing struggled with a full bucket of water, half of it sloshing out over the ground as he moved from the stone well towards one of the buildings lining the fence, repeating rifles, but no running water in town he thought, filing the information away for later.

The log cabin looks of the buildings gave them a uniformity, except for what Marcus took as the keep, the grey stone of the two-story building standing out both from its size and building material.

Now that they were in the town the thrumming had grown very intense to the point where he felt it through his molars, now that it was this close. Turning in a circle he finally located the direction and eyed the building that the vibration emanated from. The sign out front read ‘Berenger – Crystal smith’.

Marcus had to have Orah read it to him, despite his success learning to speak the language he still had yet to learn how to read. “Crystal smith?” he asked, not understanding the term.

Orah motioned for him to follow and they approached the small shop “They are run by the mages” she said, and Marcus stopped to look at her as if she had gone mad “Mages?” he asked as if he hadn’t heard her correctly, she simply looked at him and nodded, he searched for a word but not finding one in his limited vocabulary, however excitement spread over his body as he not only realized the thrumming was coming from a building run by mages.

Not only did mages exist but were common enough that she spoke of them casually.

Could it be his abilities were not as unique as he thought he wondered, noticing the look on his face she stopped cocking her head.

“I know they are rare, but surely you have seen them?” she asked giving him another one of her odd looks when he asked about something that she thought was incredibly normal Marcus just shook his head

Mages he thought, fucking magic how the hell did that happen he wondered to himself, then recalling part of the story Orah had told when he had prompted her for the history, The god Gorlin had given men the power to make there will reality, could this be what she meant he thought.

Stepping up, he looked in the window. Even through the warping of the handblown glass panes, he could see shelves lined with all manner of crystals and parchments as well as pots, pans and other items he could not identify.

He opened the door and stepped inside, as he did the pull of the thrumming intensified, he crossed the threshold of the old dusty shop, the smell of ozone and wood filled his nose as he stepped across the old worn boards, he used the intensity of the vibration to guide him as he moved.

Walking up the narrow aisles of shoddily built shelves he finally came to the front of the store where next to the counter stood something that looked like a giant cooking pot with three crystals suspended over a liquid.

As he stared into the pot, he could see that the liquid was vibrating at the same resonance as the sound.

Marcus slowly approached the odd contraption, reaching out he touched one of the blue crystals and instantly the thrumming stopped causing him to step back with a start, the vibration had just stopped, for the first time in a long time his mind was completely quiet, the effect was shocking and took it a moment to recover.

“It is called a mage’s siren, we use it to attract those with the power, it helps us recruit them to the order” a voice called from behind the counter. Marcus looked up to see a large heavyset man with long grey hair and a beard to match, his dark eyes looking him over with a hint of suspicion.

“Touching it tunes the mage to its resonance, so they don’t continue to hear it” he continued conversationally as he lumbered over to the counter. “Sorry, it looked interesting, I didn’t mean to disturb it” Marcus said keeping his face neutral as the man looked Orah over and then brought his gaze back to Marcus, he stared at Marcus seeming to appraise him before shooting another look to Orah he was going to say something and then thought better of it, deciding to simply smile as he moved back towards the counter.

“It’s fine, what can I do for you folks?” he asked an amicable smile spreading across his face as he turned back to face them.

But his eyes never left Marcus as if continuing to regard him with a knowing gaze. Marcus noticed an odd dragon tattoo on his left cheek. “anything your heart desires is probably right here, feel free to look around and let me know if I can be of assistance, we also have a few spells for sale at the counter should you need them” he continued his tone still friendly despite the odd looks he shot at Marcus.

” Spells, like magic spells?” Marcus asked trying to suppress a mocking smile, the man frowned at his tone.

“Of course, this is a mage shop my friend, should you need help growing crops, or protecting yourself from bandits, you have come to the right place” he said, pulling a jacket from the counter, turning it inside out and showing it to Marcus.

He took the piece of clothing and studied the inner liner which was covered with symbols lined in rows along the fabric, Reaching out he touched one and instantly saw the runic character begin to glow and as he watched it spread to other characters each one illuminating before his eyes, Marcus felt the buzz of energy emanating off of them.

“Amazing” he breathed as the glow began to fade. The man looked at the jacket and then at Marcus and that look of suspicion grew as if the man could guess what Marcus saw.

Handing back the jacket the man snaked out a hand and touched Marcus lightly on his arm as the old mage made contact, he felt something like electricity jump between them and Marcus quickly pulled away.

The man looked at Orah and then back at Marcus, leaning in so that she couldn’t hear he whispered, “Why aren’t’ you branded Mage?” and Marcus stepped back looking oddly at the man.

“What are you talking about?” he answered defensively, the man studying Marcus curiously and then waived a dismissive hand.

“Let me know if you see anything you like” he finished loud enough for Orah to hear before busying himself with work at the counter, ignoring the interchange they had just had.

Orah stepped up and leaned into Marcus “what was that about?” she asked, and he waved her off dismissively “Not sure” he said and then went about looking at the contraptions and other items in the shop, his stomach tightened with nervous apprehension and he distanced himself from the proprietor what does he think he knows wondered Marcus moving to the shelves.

His eyes touched upon an iron box, the top was open and inside sat two crystals a yellow and red one, like the lanterns the red one was on a turn screw and was currently far from the other.

On each corner were blue crystals facing upward. Marcus walked over, looking at the device curiously.

“Ahhh, you appreciate our newest cooktop for the little wife I see, that my friend will boil water in moments” the large shopkeeper said, once again coming around from behind the counter as he smelled an interested customer.

“This comes right from the Crystal Smiths at Dragons Keep, the plans came last week and this is the first one I have made of them, it’s a steal at one and a half gold sovereign” he said, the man reached underneath the display table and pulled out a normal looking pot “This pot is infused with azimer crystal dust and when put near bjornite, it allows it to hover” he said, taking the pot and gently placing it over the top of the box and to Marcus’s amazement the pot hovered there, like trying to push two opposing magnets towards each other. He then noticed the blue crystals were towed inward, he thought to keep the pan from sliding off of the top of the range.

The shopkeeper sensing that Marcus was impressed, moved in for the sale. Taking a cup of water, he poured it into the pot, it shook a little but never lowered to touch the box.

The shopkeeper reached over and turned the iron knob bringing the two crystals inside closer and as he did Marcus watched as they began to glow and amazingly enough, he could feel the heat.

“No longer will you have to light a fire just to boil water, this little beauty is low maintenance and easy to use” the shop keeper finished but Marcus was already turning away. He remembered the rifles and turned back to regard the large shopkeeper.

“Excuse me, maybe you can answer a question for me” Marcus asked, the shop keeper still enamored over the possibility of making a sale nodded his head enthusiastically “what would you like to know my friend” and he waited patiently as Marcus ordered his thoughts.

“The weapons the guards were carrying, the Resin Guns?” he said as the man nodded with expert assurance. “Yes sir, I take it where you are from, they don’t have those” he asked and Marcus just nodded not wanting to try and make up a story, but the answer seemed more than plausible for the shopkeeper.

“Well, as a Crystal-Smith, we do make the ammunition for them, even though the weapon technology has been available for decades, they still are more of a government item because of availability and cost not something general public have for the most part, the ammunition is incredibly expensive” he continued and Marcus just nodded, hoping to prod him into more.

“About fifty years I think, back when the late kings grandfather held the throne, he procured the services of one of the top Crystal Engineers from Dragon’s keep.

He gave him access to the famed Kubrick chronicles where Sir Kubrick Kiolpri” he began, pausing just enough so Marcus could react to the name drop.

Marcus widened his eyes and feigned being impressed, so the shop owner went on. “documented many, many of the technologies, talked about by the first ones, The Emperor challenged the smith to adapt the theory of the firearm from the chronicles into a working weapon, he began trying to experiment with crystals adapting them to the schematics for the ammunition used in the chronicles.

After many failures he finally stumbled across a hybrid crystalline that would function as ammunition for the thing, you see those weapons require an explosion to launch the projectile and it took a lot of trial and error and many years before the crafty old smith had found the right combination.

Of course, the first test was so powerful, it ended up killing two lab assistants and his cat. But when it was all done, he had created the cartridge, a crystal resin sphere made up of three of the primary crystals I believe it’s a mixture of Dar, Marheet and Jawahir crystals, giving it the explosive power needed to eject the projectile with enough strength to pierce armor clear across a large field.

Though the exact formula is a secret” he finished, and Marcus again nodded approvingly at the keepers display of crystal knowledge.

The shop keeper tried to bring the conversation back around the range and whether they would have liked it wrapped to take home instead Marcus begged off, deciding instead to wander the store and look through the shelves.

As he wandered the shop the young boy, he had seen at the well walked over and held out his hand, in it was a black crystal its sides were smooth making it look more like a golf ball Marcus thought. He held out his hand to the boy who dropped it in Marcus’s palm.

As soon as it touched him the crystal began to vibrate and glow, the young boy watching closely. But before Marcus could say anything the young boy snatched the crystal back and ran into the back room of the shop.

Marcus looked on confused trying to understand what had just happened. He looked after the young boy and then at the shop keeper who smiled and shrugged as if to say “boys will be boys”, Marcus turned instead deciding to focus on the items along the shelf but he couldn’t shake the feeling that something very important had just happened, after a few moments he was able to force it from his mind as he looked at each device laid out in front of him.

He couldn’t believe what he was seeing, where had these crystals come from and what made them so damn special, he wondered. His mind kept wandering back to the boy and that crystal, suddenly it became hard to breath, his mind beginning to get overwhelmed he didn’t know, or understand why, he had to get out of here.

“I, I need to go outside” Marcus stammered, looking back to see the shopkeeper eyeing the two of them with renewed interest, taking his arm Orah led him out of the shop and into the sunlight.

As soon as the door had shut behind them, the young boy came out of the backroom cradling the small black crystal in his hand. The shop keeper gently took it and eyed the small rock for a moment as his eyes widened. “Go get your brother, he needs to report to the order, this is too important to trust to a raven, we will need to have this delivered in person, if this is to be believed” he said to the young boy who nodded at his father and ran off.

The shop keeper stood there staring unbelievingly at the small crystal until an older boy returned, a shadow of a beard just starting to grace his chin as the dirt and sweat of manual labor looked more like part of his skin than filth.

Looking down at the small crystal, the young man’s eyes widened to match his fathers. “Is that even possible?” he whispered, and the old shop keeper shrugged. “I don’t know, but I need you to take this to Maelen, no one else, hand it to him personally, he needs to know what we found” the shop keeper said to his oldest son.

Outside Marcus bent over, taking a few steadying breaths, something about being close to all those crystals had affected him, it took him a moment to get back under control almost like the onset of a panic attack he thought, but now that he was no longer in the proximity of so many crystals he felt better, his head was clearer.

“Are you okay?” Orah asked her look and tone concerned. “yeah, I just needed some air” he said giving her a sheepish smile. Orah nodded looking him over with a worried look on her face.

Marcus’s mouth dropped open, all else pushed from his mind as a large shadow passed overhead, he extended a trembling finger “what is that” he breathed, and Orah followed his gaze. “Looks like a trader vessel, heading for the capital, we don’t usually get them out this way, but it’s not unheard of” she finished.

Marcus openly gawked at the sight. ‘Orah, that ship is flying” he stated trying to keep his voice from cracking with excitement. He was staring at an actual flying ship, he couldn’t take his eyes off it, the sight incredible as he studied the tall masts and sleek wooden lines of the vessel as it moved off to the west, the large white sails grabbing at the wind as the wooden slats making up the hull of the vessel passed directly over top of the two.

“Marcus are you okay, surely you have seen a ship before” she said her tone concerned. “How is that even possible?” he breathed his mind still trying to comprehend the sight. Orah barked a laugh.

“Gravity crystals of course, it’s not like its magic, I mean really Marcoos, it’s not that uncommon” she finished almost admonishing him. The ship moved off, dancing along the wind as it moved off towards the west, Marcus’s eyes never leaving the vessel until it was well beyond his sight, finally becoming a simple black dot in the distance did he let his eyes focus back on his companion.

“I’m sorry, I am not used to seeing them so close” he finally said, and she shot him a suspicious look, he knew she no longer bought his traveler story, but this was not the place to talk about it. “Come on, let’s go to the keep” he said trying to change the subject.

Orah smiled and nodded “We can talk to Messenger Veric, if you are interested in the stories of where we came from” she said, and Marcus nodded enthusiastically he most definitely did want to talk to this man.

The shop had reminded him, he was no longer on his earth. Things had changed he realized his eyes drifting back up to the black spot that was a flying ship, a flying fucking ship he thought with a smile and he needed, he needed to understand more about his fellow ARC members and more importantly more about the earth he now found himself.

Orah, without her realizing it had told Marcus a story that was close enough to the actual plan of the ARC initiative, enough similarities to let him know that the proverb held some truth, now he just had to suss out how much.

Standing in front of the small stone building Marcus was reminded of many of the churches he had attended as a child though this one would have probably been more at home in England then the states, it had a very Saxon look to its architecture, the stone carefully laid in a pattern that gave it an almost impenetrable feel, there was something safe about a building that had been constructed to look like a keep or castle he thought surveying the large steep peak and slate roofing, definitely a contrast to the wood and thatch of the surrounding buildings.

Surveying the exterior of the keep he found no sign or writing that would announce what it was just the sigil above the door a picture of a shield overlaid with a sword and dagger positioned like a crucifix overtop of it. Marcus studied the symbol with a small smile at the persistence of the religious symbol shown, etched into the stone.

Stepping up to the large wooden door, Orah pulled it open with very little strain the doors sliding smoothly along well-oiled hinges and with a gesture, she motioned Marcus inside.

Entering he couldn’t help but be reminded of the churches of his youth. The large rectangular room was lined with a single burgundy carpet down the center and on either side stood long worn wooden pews facing forward towards a simple wooden podium atop a dais on the far end of the room.

It looked very much like every church of his youth Marcus thought walking quietly up the aisle towards the podium. Stepping up onto the dais he regarded the large Mural of a King, his face kindly and all-knowing as he sat upon a large golden throne his eyes looking out over the pews giving a pleasant fatherly look.

“That is Aurtus, our emissary to the gods” Orah whispered as she too stepped onto the wooden dais.

“It’s an approximation of our Emissary, though I think it’s a bit grand” came a reedy but pleasant voice from one side of the large chamber. Marcus turned surprised as a tall thin man quietly closed a door that he had not previously noticed.

Marcus could see he wore a long black robe; the blonde hair was cut short and shot through with a generous amount of grey. His blue eyes sparkled with humor and a smile that was very warm and welcoming.

“I am messenger Veric” he introduced himself, Marcus absently held out his hand, Veric reached over and clasped his wrist, Marcus was surprised for a moment but quickly recovered and did the same.

“I am Marcus” he said slightly bowing and doing his best to avoid calling this man Father as was ingrained into him from his days of attending Catholic mass with his parents.

He nodded and then turned to face Orah “It is good to see you Orah, we have missed you since your parents passed, I was hoping you would rejoin us” he said embracing her and she returned the gesture.

“Thank you, Messenger, I wonder if you have some time, Marcoos wishes to find out more about Aurtus and the stories of the beginning of the Second Age, he is from somewhere far away and is interested in our culture” she explained. Veric cocked his head “A place that doesn’t have Wic, well how can I resist introducing someone to the wonders of Aurtus” he said and gestured for them to follow.

He walked back towards the door he had come in and ushered the two through it. They entered a small chamber with a bed and a table that sat next to a window overlooking a beautiful garden.

“Please sit, I will make us some tea” he said motioning the two over towards the small wooden table. Marcus and Orah each took a seat as the man busied himself at a counter. The room was cozy and aside from the simple furniture there was very little personal about the space.

Marcus wondered if it had to do with a vow, like the vow of poverty but wasn’t sure how to ask it. “So, Marcus you are interested in where we come from? I take it your own stories differ from the ones that Orah has regaled you with?” Veric asked glancing at Marcus who nodded, the messenger smiling kindly as he turned back to brewing tea.

A sweet but pungent odor filled Marcus’s nostrils; it was pleasant but aromatic.

“I am very interested in hearing the stories of Origin, Orah has told me some of the tales and I wish to know more” he stated.

Part of him felt guilty lying to a holy man, but that was the catholic in him he thought and dismissed it.

The older man continued to make the tea, once he was done, he cradled the three mugs in his arms and carried them over to the table, placing one in front of each of them as he sat down and joined them, quietly regarding Marcus for a moment.

“So, Marcus where do you hail from?” he asked innocently. “I come from across the sea, we have recently built boats to sail to new lands, mine is called Germany” he said and had almost a moment of panic as he recalled the flying ship, did they sail, was it called something else, did they even use the sea he wondered and then forced it down, keeping the mask of a smile on his face, the man clapped excitedly, not noticing Marcus’s moment of doubt.

“I had heard a few of the far nations had successfully built vessels that could cross the open sea, I am excited to meet someone from one of those lands perhaps one day I will travel across the great sea to deliver the word of Aurtus to places like this Germany” he said excitedly, his eyes unfocused as he imagined the man was thinking of the possibilities and another pang of guilt washed through him.

Internally he sighed with relief, he had gone out on a bit of a limb not really knowing if they had begun to spread out and travel to other lands, he had gotten lucky.

Sipping at the tea the flavor was fruity like apple with a mild spice and Marcus nodded in approval. Veric smiled appreciating the silent compliment.

“So, I am going to assume you don’t know anything, if I cover something you do know, please feel free to stop me” he began, and Marcus leaned in listening intently.

“The gods, there are four of them, each is an elemental charged with reigning and protecting our land.” He began

“There is Aquis, god of water and life, Aria goddess of Air and the hunt, Juo god of the land and the harvest, sometimes called god of thunder and lightning and finally Gorlin god of fire and creation” he continued and Marcus nodded, they have created an entirely new religion since he had left he thought wondering what had happened to the religions I remember, probably the same thing that seems to happen to everything else he thought morbidly, turned to dust.

Veric leaned in and regarded the two, using the pause to collect his thoughts before continuing his lecture.

“During the first age, man, like the gods before them created life, this life took the shape of machines that could think and work, these machines did everything for man allowing them to turn their minds to loftier pursuits and ideals, however in doing that they raised themselves in their own minds to the level of the gods and ignored the old lessons, scarring the planet for resources, dirtying the water and poisoning the land, the gods grew angry and at the behest of the fifth god Mephis” Marcus stopped him “fifth god?, but there are only four you said” he inquired.

Veric nodded “I know, I will explain” he stated Marcus making a motion for the man to continue,

Veris nodded enthusiastically like most men of god talking about his religion excited him “Mephis was an old god, one who did not like or trust humans while the others watched humanity he stood back despising those who had ruined there creation he bore witness to how the humans treated the world and grew angry, Mephis convinced the four to cast out man and they did, destroying humanity and removing any sign they existed, it had been Mephis’s proudest moment, all monuments to their great civilization were laid to ash in an instant”

Marcus stopped him for a moment “does it say how they did this?” he asked Veric shrugged “It is said Gorlin was commissioned to create a great machine, a death machine and that this was brought to earth, mankind being the curious creatures had activated it, they had architected their own demise” he answered, “Many scholars have debated whether the machine actually existed and if so, how had it so effectively destroyed man and all its inventions” Veric mused not noticing the look on Marcus’s face as it stood crestfallen.

The Messenger continued to look into the distance smiling as he continued his story. “After a few millennia the gods grew lonely, Juo and Aria decided to return man, gathering the souls of the dead they set about creating new bodies for them and, Juo then traveled far into the universe where she found the Tergorimon the great snake responsible for moving the planets and moons, harvesting some of its scales, Juo presented them to Gorlin, the forge master,

Gorlin made them into small containers, able to survive the fires of the sky and used them to house man, protecting them as they were sent back to earth. However the gods, did not want to repeat the past and stripped humans of the ability to create the great machines and buildings, forcing them to live in harmony with the land, this was not easy as man had forgotten the simple lessons of survival and many died in the early days, this was called the age of darkness.

Mephis however was furious and damned the gods for returning man to the paradise that earth had now become.

He tried to force man off the planet, sending a plague that killed many, but the other gods intervened, banding together they cast Mephis to the underworld, beyond the sight of man or the heavens where even now he remains trapped, but that is another story” he said,

“So how long ago did man return in the metal tears?” Marcus inquired but sure he didn’t want to hear the answer “Well when they returned it was called, as I said, the Age of Darkness, since man had yet to realize the gifts the gods had left them, so if I were to hazard a guess maybe a thousand years” Veric postulated.

It felt like someone had punched Marcus in the gut and he had to take a few deep breaths in order to keep from panicking or hyperventilating, Sentinel had given him a loose timeline, but hearing this man speak caused a panic.

Veric didn’t seem to notice as he was wrapped up in continuing his story. “You see Gorlin, seeing man struggle had decided to bestow a gift upon them, taking the great spirit crystals from the heavens, he shattered them upon his anvil and spread them over the earth, giving man a little of his blood he bestowed the ability to manifest their thoughts into reality, to draw the gods power from the crystals and use it.

This is called ‘The Gift of Gorlin’ now over the generations it was not passed to everyone, but those who receive it are usually taken to the Order of the Dragon, the order of Mages who train those with such gifts, “Veric finished.

Marcus nodded, thinking of his own ability but deciding to keep it quiet. “Tell me more about the crystals and these gifts” he asked his eyes imploring the Messenger, Veric smiled and continued.
