“Mages draw power from crystals, we are not sure how, they have the ability to direct that energy applying it to there will and allowing them to manipulate elements and even move objects without touching them” Veric said

“When man first returned they banded together into small tribes, these tribes immediately began to fight over the one resource they had, knowledge, those within the tribes who had knowledge to create, build or design things that could help the tribe were targeted either for death or taken by another stronger tribe” Veric paused to ensure everyone was listening.

“Now the interesting part of the story is, during these decades of fighting an Emperor emerged, Aurtus, who, after years of strife, brought together all of the tribes of man under his rule, conquering the other leaders to become ruler of all of man, he kept peace within the tribes of man for decades and as he grew older, the gods were so impressed by his accomplishments they decided upon his death to raise him up and he became our emissary to the gods, thus why we celebrate Emissary Aurtus to this day” he finished smiling at the two of them. Marcus managed to smile back but it came out as more a lopsided grin.

The stories had not helped, he felt more alone now then he had prior to coming into the keep, he was a man out of time, a man without a home he realized, but maybe he did have a home, a small spark of hope emerged as he thought of his abilities.

He looked to the Messenger and leaned in “What can you tell me about the mages?” he asked thinking of the shop keeper with the strange tattoo. Veric nodded.

“Once, upon our return to this land, we were all mages bestowed with great power, however over the years the power has diminished and less and less of those born have the gift.

About two hundred years ago a group of Magi banded together and began to terrorize and rob the land, the group of leaders called the triad believed that since they had power, they should rule and set out to make that happen.

The Emperor at that time approached the church to help end the terror. So, the church turned to a group of peaceful mages, with the help of this group they set about creating and crafting weapons and armor to aid them in mitigating the powers of the mages, they trained mage assassins, groups of men specifically trained to neutralize and kill mages, the war did not last long after that, the church began to hunt down this rogue group, eliminating them” Veric continued and then hesitated for a moment, his excited face falling.

“But it did not stop there, the inquisitor as he was named decided that all those with the power were a blight and tried to destroy any who showed power, it brought the church into a three-way war, the triad, the church and the group of mages who had aided them in creating the weapons and armor headed by a woman named Zathris.

The war threatened to end life as we knew it, it was a dark time for the church, finally the Lord Reagent, the head of the church put a stop to it and in a historic meeting, Zathris, Corlin, the Lord Reagent at the time and Emperor Augustus set down and wrote what we now call the Agreement, the land still feared the Magi, so the Emperor decreed any born with the gift would be marked with a symbol” He stated.

Marcus thought about the dragon tattoo and nodded, now it made sense. “In an effort to protect those magi left, Zathris created the Order of the Dragon with the blessing of the king, the order takes those who display power at a young age and trains them to use their power,

The magi are also responsible for policing their own. However, each generation is less powerful than the one before, I imagine before long there will be no more Mages left in the world” he finished, and Marcus got the sense the man was not saddened by this.

“Thank you, Messenger, I appreciate your time” Marcus said as Veric nodded “Please stay for assembly, you might learn something” he said. At first, Marcus begged off, but the man was convincing. The next hour saw Marcus and Orah sitting in the middle pew as assembly began.

Sitting there among the community Marcus looked around noticing something he had never seen during his time as a catholic. Among the crowd sat many couple’s men and women, men and men and women and women.

He smiled and closed his eyes whispering a thank you to those who had been able to guide the second reign of humanity to allow all people to be welcome within the religion.

As they left the church, Marcus leaned in toward Orah. “I noticed there was a lot of different types of couples, the church allows this.

Orah looking at him with an odd expression one he had begun to get used to, the same look he would get if he wondered why the sky was blue and she said. “the gods make people how they are, it is not for us to judge them, all people are from the gods so all people are as they should be” she answered as if that was the most obvious thing in the world.

Marcus nodded to her “Yes they are” he simply said still smiling glad he could find things in this strange new world that gave him hope.

They stopped at the general store as Orah picked up supplies, paying the man with two gold coins, both having the picture of a woman on one side and a lioness on the other. “What are those coins?” he asked as they left.

She pulled another out and showed it to him. “This is the currency of the realm, that is our Empress, Victoria and on the other side is her sigil the lioness” she finished and put the coin away. Marcus nodded the two leaving town, but Marcus was determined to come back, he liked Veric and thought he still had a lot to learn, but the experience in the Crystal Smith’s shop had forced caution upon him.

The shopkeeper had known what he was, the question was what he would do with that information Marcus mused.

He pushed it to the back of his mind for now, he didn’t want to worry Orah about something he had no answer for, besides they had harvest to worry about if they were to survive the winter.

With that he smiled at how simple his life had become and looked at the beautiful woman next to him and for the first time he realized,

he could come to like this life.
